P.h: BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day exploited since late August
P.p: A critical auth bypass and arbitrary file upload flaw, scored 9.3 CVSS, hits BeyondTrust Remote Support 26.2.3 and earlier. Unauthenticated attackers can perform file operations, escalate to root and reach credential vaults. Suspected Chinese state-sponsored group Armory Castle (UNC5221) has used it since late August to drop custom webshells such as BARECLAW.
P.s: BeyondTrust shipped patches in October for self-hosted customers. CISA and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security advise restricting external access to the appliances and running forensic reviews for signs of compromise.

items.h: Meta Muse share links expose 6,800 conversations
items.d: Claroc found them via passive DNS, because conversation titles sit in subdomains. Samples showed bank-fraud details, loan applications and revenue reviews. Meta paused sharing on October 20.

items.h: Hacker used AI agents to breach 100+ sites in about 23 hours
items.d: Open-source Cairn panels were reportedly used against John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins. NorForge found 20+ exposed panels. Trufflehog found hundreds of secrets, 11% verified valid.

items.h: Romulus ClickFix platform delivers Legion Loader
items.d: Fake landing pages trick users into running commands. PowerShell scripts then deploy trojanized MSI installers or encrypted archives. Six IP addresses run the platform.

items.h: Eight compromised TLS certificates put the internet on alert
items.d: Intermediate certs from India-based CA eMudhra were defective at a level engineers thought impossible, per TLDR's quick links.

P.h: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats
P.p: Microsoft added Guardian Agents and agent detection in Defender to protect enterprises from AI agents acting as insider threats. CEO Satya Nadella and security chief Hayete Gallot warned that frontier models cannot be trusted because they are unpredictable and lack organizational norms.
P.s: Their advice: separate the supply of intelligence from authority over it, using independent monitoring. TLDR IT's analysis pieces add that good automation targets are reversible, bounded and observable.

tiles.t: Lambda Web Functions are public by default
tiles.d: No auth, and role credentials sit in environment variables. Existing lambda:* grants may cover them, and SCPs and tooling may miss shadow functions.

tiles.t: PHP warns of two critical RCE flaws
tiles.d: Emergency patches due tomorrow. Believed to affect PHP 5 through 8.
Splits fetch and install phases, adds Landlock and Seatbelt sandboxes. Go and Elm remove code execution entirely.
Copied commands are scrubbed of PII and checked by Safe Browsing. Gemini scam detection moves server-side.

tiles.t: DHS bans DeepSeek in civilian agencies
tiles.d: Cites data possibly stored in China. 60 days to request exceptions.

P.h: Anthropic replaces Git with Scion for its monorepo
P.p: Anthropic built Scion, a centralized source control system for tens of millions of daily CI checkouts. Content-addressed storage, server-side repository operations and tiered caches cut source-control CPU and memory footprint 200 times versus its previous Git mirroring setup.
P.s: Elsewhere in TLDR DevOps: Cloudflare cut its AI code reviewer cost from $2.43 to $0.77 per review with shared prompt-cache prefixes and fewer redundant tool calls, though cheaper setups missed some findings.

tiles.d: Cloudflare and VoidZero report up to 8x faster and about 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0. Runs in WebAssembly.
Managed ingress that provisions load balancers and certificates. Up to 25 services share one ALB.
Operators for deterministic reconciliation, agents for unclear paths. Phase autonomy from read-only to approved low-risk changes.
Turnkey threat detection for Kubernetes, in preview.
Local tool compresses logs and JSON, reportedly 20% fewer tokens for coding agents.

items.h: 970,000 Medi-Cal members hit by Paradigm Healthcare breach
items.d: Access between October 8 and 15, 2025 exposed names, birth dates, gender and member IDs.
The draft prospectus cites uncertain compute access and risk factors on preventing model harm. It signals possible spend of $750 billion on compute.

items.h: Google Cloud London power failure hits Cloud Run, GKE, Kafka
items.d: Banking, delivery and property services were disrupted, showing how one zone failure ripples across businesses.

items.h: AWS TorchNeuron brings native PyTorch to Trainium
items.d: Public beta. Amazon will also contribute upstream to make PyTorch less CUDA-centric.
